title: The Sleepy Dragon
story:
A small dragon named Pebble slept on the roof of a village bakery. He was the size of a large dog, and his scales were the color of warm bread. Pebble loved the heat from the ovens and the smell of butter. The baker, Hana, did not fear him, because he was gentle. Each morning she left a roll on the chimney ledge. In return, Pebble kept noisy pigeons away from the cooling racks. On cold days, his breath warmed the kitchen just enough.

One winter morning, Pebble slept through Hana's usual knock. The ovens stayed cool, and the first customers found the door shut. Hana climbed a ladder and tapped his nose with a wooden spoon. Pebble opened one eye, sneezed a cloud of flour, and looked sorry. He slid down to the yard and blew a careful flame into the stove. The fire caught, and the kitchen filled with a comfortable heat. Hana baked extra rolls and gave Pebble two, not one.

The customers waited in the yard and laughed at the flour on his nose. A child asked if the dragon was dangerous. Hana said he was only dangerous to cold rooms and rude pigeons. Pebble yawned, climbed back to the roof, and fell asleep again. The village agreed to let him stay for as long as he wished.
